E01_capacity.conclusion: The 30-cell FULL16 frame carries 120 raw bits, of which 88 are payload (11 bytes). At 60 display frames/s the raw rate is 7200 bps, the framed payload rate is 5280 bps, and the RS(255,223) goodput is 4617 bps. A packet occupies 4.25 s at 60 fps and the 4-bit packet id caps a transfer at 16 packets (39216 bytes before compression). These are THEORETICAL arithmetic values; software timings are OBSERVED on the run machine.
E01_capacity.title: Protocol arithmetic and raw capacity

E02_patterns.conclusion: Measured mean target-cell accuracy by severity: brutal=0.314, clean=1.000, extreme=1.000, harsh=1.000, mild=1.000. The 16-way decision was perfect in clean, extreme, harsh, mild; it degraded in brutal (figures above and per-pattern rows in the CSV). FULL16 has minimum Hamming distance 1 between cell symbols, so a single misclassified triangle changes the decoded nibble. This is why the protocol adds a CRC-16 per frame and RS(255,223) per packet instead of relying on the cell alphabet for protection.

summary.note: FULL16 uses all 16 combinations, so the minimum symbol distance is one triangle (1 bit). There is no intra-cell error correction; detection and correction rely on the frame CRC and RS layer.

E02_patterns.title: Separability of the 16 four-triangle cell patterns

E03_frame_robustness.conclusion: A failure boundary was measured for 2 of 8 parameters (brightness first failed at 0.08; perspective first failed at 0.18). No failure was reached within the tested range for blur_sigma, noise_sigma, jpeg_quality, ambient, vignette, gamma; the per-frame photometric calibration makes global brightness, gamma and ambient offset largely irrelevant until contrast is destroyed. Blur mixes triangle interiors, noise perturbs the per-cell threshold, JPEG creates block artefacts, perspective stresses fiducial detection, and vignetting reduces corner contrast. These are SIMULATED observations, not physical camera results; the exact crossing points are in processed/summary.csv.

summary.success_rule: frame CRC-16 matches after spatial decode

E03_frame_robustness.title: Single-frame decode robustness sweep

E04_geometry.conclusion: The last fully successful downscale was 0.06 (8.6 effective px per cell) and the first failure was 0.04 (5.7 px per cell). Perspective stayed correct up to 0.12 and first failed at 0.16. Resolution loss makes triangle sampling windows overlap pattern boundaries; perspective is limited by the fiducial detector's fixed area/aspect gates and quadrant assumption, which are tuned for a cropped screen. The exact crossing points are in the per-trial CSV. The perspective sweep is an angle proxy, not a measurement of a real phone at a real angle.
E04_geometry.title: Resolution (distance proxy) and perspective (angle proxy)

E05_erasures.conclusion: With nsym=32, packets decode with up to 32 lost frames; the smallest failing loss count observed is 33. This matches the theoretical erasure capacity of 32 per RS block because interleaving turns each lost frame into exactly one erasure in every block. Random and burst loss behave the same at equal counts under byte interleaving.

summary.interleaving: frame n carries byte n of every block, so a lost frame is one erasure per block

E05_erasures.title: Frame loss and Reed-Solomon erasure capacity

E06_errors.conclusion: The measured boundary follows 2*errors + erasures <= nsym. Cases at or below capacity decode; cases above it fail with E_ECC/E_RECONSTRUCT rather than returning corrupt data. This is an injected-error test of the RS layer, not an optical measurement: frame CRC would normally convert most optical byte errors into erasures.
E06_errors.title: Reed-Solomon byte-error and mixed error/erasure capacity

E07_compression.conclusion: OTL1 compresses repetitive, textual and structured payloads strongly (highest mean ratio: zeros at 58.5×), leaves incompressible random data at roughly unit ratio (mean 0.984 (range 0.972–0.992)), and always round-trips byte-exactly. Because the compressed payload determines the number of packets, compression directly reduces screen time. OTL1 does not claim to beat zlib/zstd on general data; its purpose is a small, deterministic, inspectable instruction stream.

summary.note: OTL1 is a deterministic, dependency-free dictionary codec designed for the on-screen instruction set; zlib/zstd numbers are references, not part of the protocol. Each size is generated independently, so the random corpus is not compressible by block repetition.

E07_compression.title: Shared instruction dictionary (OTL1) compression effectiveness

E08_rolling.conclusion: A 26-chip word is recovered only when the rolling readout spans at least 26 display symbol periods; the lowest tested display rate with a fitting word was 1000 Hz. At 60 Hz a 27.0 ms readout sees ~1.62 symbols, so a full blink word cannot fit in one capture. Separately, 3 trial(s) had a fitting readout but an exposure up to 2.50 symbol periods long; integrating several chips per row destroyed the word. Exposure must therefore be no longer than one symbol period as well as the readout spanning the word. This is the central temporal constraint of the proposed architecture, and it is a physical/arithmetic result, not a software limitation.

summary.physical_limit: visible display symbols = height * row_time / symbol_period; camera frame rate does not multiply display refresh rate; exposure must also be no longer than one symbol period

E08_rolling.title: Temporal blink IDs under a rolling-shutter capture

E09_end_to_end.conclusion: 48 of 64 simulated transfers succeeded (75.0%); 16 failed. Successes by channel: clean 16/16, mild 16/16, harsh 16/16, brutal 0/16. Failures: brutal 16/16; stages frame_crc×16, packet×16, reassembly×16. All 64 payload SHA-256 values were checked against the pre-run manifest (64/64 matched) and re-derived from the recorded generator specification (64/64 identical); payload manifest 9cf02deb1f14…, outcome fingerprint c4d98b2becdd…. Throughput (successful trials only): simulated net 3953.5 bps and projected 60 fps net 3529.4 bps. Latency: spatial decode 8.57 ms per decoded frame, total pipeline 8982 ms per trial. Reconstruction: reassembly+decompress 0.03 ms, RS ECC 3.36 ms per trial. Resources: 181% CPU of one core, peak RSS 183552 KiB. These are SIMULATED / SOFTWARE results, not a physical optical transmission benchmark.

latency.basis: all trials; per-decoded-frame spatial decode time and total pipeline time

summary.note: SIMULATED / SOFTWARE. Simulated wall time is Python execution time; projected screen time = frames / 60 fps. Neither is a physical camera measurement. All trials, including failures, are retained in raw/trials.jsonl.

reconstruction_time.basis: all trials; reassembly + decompression, and Reed-Solomon ECC

throughput.basis: successful trials only; simulated execution and projected 60 fps screen time

E09_end_to_end.title: End-to-end simulated transfer

E10_determinism.conclusion: Rendering is byte-identical across repeated calls, decoding the same prerecorded PNGs twice produces identical cell sequences, and the end-to-end pipeline reproduces the same drop pattern and output with a fixed seed. The decoder has no camera dependency. Latency and memory figures are OBSERVED software measurements on this host and will vary with hardware.
E10_determinism.title: Determinism, prerecorded-image decoding and resource benchmark

E11_physical.conclusion: PHYSICAL / CAMERA CAPTURE. Session m10-baseline-01-20261108T112241Z from iPhone14,2 (Continuity Camera, 'Arsh Camera') capturing a Apple M5 built-in Liquid Retina (MacBook Air): 888 camera samples, 549 passed the frame CRC (61.8%); 255/255 unique displayed frames (100.0%). Mean cell accuracy 1.000 and bit accuracy 1.000 over 255 unique frames with a display mapping. A complete payload of 317 bytes was recovered from 294 compressed bytes (1.08x) and its SHA-256 matched the transmitted payload. At the observed 10.00 display fps the gross channel rate is 1200 bps, the gross payload rate is 880 bps, the RS(255,223) goodput is 769 bps and the SHA-verified application rate is 99 bps. Decode latency 7.09 ms per camera sample, packet decode + reassembly 2.15 ms, decode throughput 141.1 samples/s. All physical numbers come from the preserved camera files; decoding is software. Compare with E01–E10 only through the comparison table, which states the basis of every pair.

E12_channel_efficiency.conclusion: PHYSICAL / CAMERA CAPTURE. E12 analysed 7 finalized session(s); 4 delivered the complete SHA-verified payload. Baseline repeats: 3 session(s), repeatable=True (throughput CV 0.0). For the reference transfer the gross channel rate is 1199.88 bps, gross payload 879.91 bps, RS(255,223) goodput 769.49 bps and application throughput 99.44 bps. The application carries 1.243 bytes per displayed frame out of 11 (11.30%). From the gross channel to the application the total gap is 1100.44 bps: framing 319.97 bps, RS parity 110.42 bps, unused packet capacity 677.27 bps, with compression recovering 7.21 bps. The narrower RS-to-application gap is 670.05 bps (unused packet capacity minus compression gain). The dominant loss is application payload utilisation (unused packet capacity) at 677.27 bps (56.4% of the gross channel). Camera capture and decode have measured headroom; RS corrections and packet loss are zero; detection/CRC failures did not reduce unique-frame delivery. Across the three independent baselines, unique-frame delivery ranged 0.965-1.000 and camera-sample CRC rate ranged 0.618-0.889, yet all three recovered the exact payload; the one baseline that lost 9 frames was repaired by 18 RS symbols. The panel ran at 9.999 fps, not 60 Hz; the 6x difference is a playback choice, and 60 fps values are projections, not measurements. Brightness was set and read back at [0.65, 0.9] fractions, but both brightness sessions lost the fiducials to hand-held framing drift after about 14 s ([455, 457] detection failures; unique-frame delivery [0.686, 0.573]), so no brightness effect is claimed; that is a measured receiver reliability failure, not a brightness result. Distance, angle and ambient illuminance remain UNMEASURED. All measured numbers come from preserved camera files; projections are labelled separately.

E13_packet_utilisation.conclusion: PHYSICAL / CAMERA CAPTURE. E13 analysed 5 successful locked M11 session(s). The frozen 317-byte transfer uses 11.99% of the 2453-byte packet data region; the rest is zero padding. The highest measured wire-limited application throughput was 792.39 bps in m11-a5-rs24-20261108T123758Z (A5_rs24), a 7.97x gain over the frozen 99.44 bps. The dictionary arm recovered 145,745 application bytes in one packet at 45705.64 bps of pre-compression application bytes (its wire payload rate is 758.91 bps); the higher application figure is compression gain, not extra wire capacity. Arms without a successful physical session: A4_always_on. Every successful arm matched its SHA-256 manifest; erasures and RS corrections are reported per session. Software arms that have no locked physical session are not promoted to measurements.

root_cause.explanation: The packet is always 255 frames x 11 bytes = 2,453 RS data bytes. The frozen payload is only 317 application bytes (294 wire bytes after OTL1), so 2,159 of the 2,453 data bytes are zero padding. 11.99% is unused capacity, not loss: the packet is shorter than its container, and the padding is still RS-encoded and transmitted.
